faq.a: Zahida is associated with the Arabic form زَاهِدَة, whose core sense is zahida; ascetic (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Zahida?
faq.a: Zahida is associated with Arabic. Zahida is Arabic زَاهِدَة (Zāhida), the feminine of زَاهِد, meaning 'ascetic'.
Yes — the underlying form زَاهِدَة is Arabic.
Zahida can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zahida should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zāhida is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zahida mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zahida is rendered زاہدہ and carries the sense زاہدہ، پرہیزگار.

faq.q: What does Zahida mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zahida is rendered زاهده and carries the sense زاهده، پارسا.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-hi-da. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zahida?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zahida, zahida. Script forms are زاهده, زاہدہ, زَاهِدَة, ज़ाहिदा.

faq.q: Is Zahida a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
